title: Crop, Straighten, and AI-Expand in Photoshop (Day 13) — Composition via Crop Tool
summary: In Day 13 of PHLEARN’s 30 Days of Photoshop, the instructor demonstrates how to crop and straighten an image and then expand the canvas using AI to improve composition. The lesson emphasizes starting with a crooked horizon, choosing and adjusting crop ratios (including square 1:1 and film-like sizes), and using overlays such as rule of thirds and golden spiral to plan placement of subjects. The video contrasts manual straightening via the horizon-drag/rotate approach with the built-in Straighten tool, and shows how to toggle crop shield opacity and reset fixed ratios with the Clear button. A major focus is the Generative Expand AI fill, which can extend the image beyond its original bounds and generate variations in real time to create a more balanced composition. The instructor demonstrates reapplying overlays after AI expansion and iterating between square and other aspect ratios to achieve a final, more intentional crop with improved space around the subjects, guided by compositional rules (rule of thirds, golden spiral) but ultimately flexible to user intent.

sections.title: Crop shield and freeform adjustments

sections.title: Horizon straightening via crop rotate

sections.title: Alternative straightening: Straighten tool

sections.title: Free-cropping with composition planning
sections.description: Continuing crop with ratio-free control, applying rule of thirds or switching to other ratios (like 16x9) to plan composition while preserving subject placement.

sections.title: Overlay tools: Golden Spiral for composition
sections.description: Introducing the golden spiral overlay as an alternative compositional aid to guide the viewer’s eye through the image.
